children: The partnership will scale a bio-based fuel technology for heavy-duty sectors including transport, agriculture, mining and construction

Praj Industries and Gevo, Inc. have entered into a partnership to advance Bio-IBA technology for diesel blending in India, targeting applications across heavy-fuel-consuming industries. The collaboration will give Praj exclusive rights to scale and commercialise Gevo’s Bio-IBA technology in the Indian market.
The companies said the initiative represents the first application of Bio-IBA for diesel blending, creating a potential pathway for incorporating renewable carbon into conventional fuel use.

Under the agreement, Praj Industries will lead the scaling and commercialisation of Gevo’s Bio-IBA technology across India. The partnership combines Gevo’s bio-based technology with Praj’s experience in processing sugar- and starch-based feedstocks, engineering and project execution.
The arrangement is aimed at developing the technology for use in India’s heavy-fuel market, where diesel remains an important energy source across several economic activities.
The proposed applications span transportation, agriculture, mining and construction, along with other industries that depend significantly on diesel and other conventional fuels.

The companies are positioning Bio-IBA as a potential route to introduce renewable carbon into diesel blending. The approach is intended to support lower-carbon fuel pathways without changing the broader industrial sectors in which diesel is used.

For heavy-duty applications, where alternatives to conventional liquid fuels can be more difficult to deploy, bio-based fuel technologies are increasingly being explored as part of broader decarbonisation efforts.
The collaboration brings together Gevo’s technology platform and Praj’s capabilities in feedstock processing and project execution.
Praj has experience working with sugar- and starch-based feedstocks, while Gevo has developed bio-based technologies aimed at producing renewable alternatives for fuel and chemical applications.
The companies will use these capabilities to pursue the scale-up and commercial deployment of Bio-IBA technology in India.

The partnership also reflects growing interest in technologies that can introduce renewable carbon into established fuel markets. Its focus on diesel blending could provide an alternative pathway for sectors where conventional fuels continue to play a significant role.

The commercial potential of the technology will depend on its ability to scale economically and integrate with existing fuel and industrial systems. The companies have not disclosed specific investment or capacity targets under the agreement.
Praj Industries and Gevo will work to scale Bio-IBA technology in India, focusing on diesel blending and heavy-fuel applications across multiple industries.
